title: VIGOR: Benchmarking Visual Rationale Correctness in Multimodal Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.13150v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are typically evaluated by whether they produce correct answers, but correctness alone does not reveal whether their outputs are supported by the right visual evidence. We introduce VIGOR, a benchmark for evaluating VIsually GrOunded Rationales in MLLMs. VIGOR represents visual rationales as explicit concepts paired with pixel-level groundings, covering multiple abstraction levels including low-level visual properties, intermediate structures, objects, parts and high-level motion, relations. To construct VIGOR at scale, we develop an automatic annotation framework that reuses existing dense supervision when available and generates missing concept groundings through proposal-based annotation followed by conservative multimodal verification. translated_title: VIGOR：多模态大语言模型视觉推理依据正确性的基准测试
translated_abstract: 多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）通常以是否给出正确答案来评估，但仅凭答案正确并不能揭示其输出是否得到了正确视觉证据的支持。我们提出了VIGOR，一个用于评估MLLMs视觉接地推理依据的基准。VIGOR将视觉推理依据表示为显式概念与像素级接地区域的配对，涵盖多个抽象层次，包括低层视觉属性、中间结构、物体、部件以及高层运动和关系。为了大规模构建VIGOR，我们开发了一个自动标注框架，该框架在可用时复用现有的密集监督标注，并通过基于候选区域的标注加保守的多模态验证来生成缺失的概念接地区域。利用VIGOR，我们通过比较模型对每个所表达概念给出的视觉证据与标注的接地区域，来评估MLLMs是否“言出必看”（即是否真正关注其答案所依据的视觉区域）。
tldr: VIGOR提出了一个通过将视觉推理依据的显式概念与像素级接地区域配对、跨越多个抽象层次，来评估多模态大语言模型是否真正“看着自己所说的内容”（即其答案是否由正确视觉证据支持）的基准测试。
en_tdlr: VIGOR is a benchmark that evaluates whether multimodal large language models "look at what they say" by pairing explicit visual rationale concepts with pixel-level groundings across multiple abstraction levels, using an automatic annotation framework with conservative multimodal verification.
